name: spend a fixed budget, then write what each unit earned
one_line: A fixed number of tokens, three uses that pay differently and are capped, and afterwards a line saying what every single token brought in.
how: Print three uses with a yield and a cap — five a token up to four tokens, three up to six, two up to ten — and hand over twelve tokens. Ask for the distribution and its total first. Only underneath print the counts: thirty-two distributions exist, the best is 42, the worst 26, and half of them reach 34. Then the line that carries the sheet: write what each of the twelve tokens earned, in order. It comes out 5 5 5 5 3 3 3 3 3 3 2 2, and that falling row is opportunity cost with no definition and no arithmetic past subtraction. The caps are fixed here: without them the answer is put everything on the best one, and the row never falls.

knobs.effect: Three uses that pay the same turn thirty-two distributions into one outcome, and the resource is still printed but has stopped existing. Unequal yields with caps are what make the sheet a decision rather than a rite.

knobs.knob: an exact total or the largest one
knobs.effect: «Reach exactly ten» produces a choice; «score as much as you can» produces volume and reads as a score. The first is fixed here, because a total nobody is trying to maximise cannot turn into a running tally.
Numbers on the page make it arithmetic and cost nobody anything. Tokens that buy real pieces of the afternoon make it a resource, and then somebody in the house has to have something to give.
Above the blanks they are the answer and the distribution gets copied off them. Below, they are a term of comparison for something already written, and nothing on the page can be worked backwards.

where_the_work_is: In the price list. A number beside a thing says what counts more plainly than a sentence does, and leaves it open to being disagreed with, which a line of encouragement does not.
breaks: The paper cannot stop anybody writing thirteen tokens; it registers and does not forbid, and this record leans on that instead of pretending otherwise. Nothing carries to the next afternoon and nothing here asks it to. Scanned back, a column of single digits reads only if the rows are set well apart. On 800x480 the four-column table does not fit; the row of twelve numbers does, and it is the half worth showing.
